events.text: A magistrate is holding a poetry contest at the Pavilion of Falling Plums. The prize is a jade brush and, more importantly, an audience with half the scholars of the province.

choices.text: Enter with a poem about the mountains

ok.log: Your poem is read aloud twice. The magistrate asks for a copy. By autumn, strangers are quoting you in teahouses.

fail.log: Your poem rhymes 'mountain' with 'mountain'. A child in the audience points this out.

effects.log: You listen to the best poets in the province. On the walk home, lines start arriving in your head.

events.text: A tongue-tied young swordsman begs you to write a love letter for him. 'You have a way with words. I have a way with... swords.'

ok.log: The letter works. At the wedding, the bride tells you, quietly, that she knew who really wrote it. She married him anyway.

fail.log: The letter is so overwrought that the young lady returns it with corrections. In red ink.

choices.text: Tell him to speak from the heart

effects.log: He stammers his way through a confession. It is terrible. It works.

events.text: A new restaurant owner asks you to paint the signboard for her shop. Whatever you write, the whole street will read for years.

choices.text: Paint it with your best brushwork

ok.log: Your characters are so strong that people come to eat just to look at the sign. The owner feeds you free for life.

fail.log: It is legible. That is the nicest thing anyone says about it.

choices.text: Decline: you are a martial artist, not a painter

effects.log: She hires a scholar. His sign is beautiful. You feel oddly jealous.

events.text: An old monk at the roadside shrine has a Go board and no opponent. 'Win,' he says, 'and I will tell you a secret about your martial art.'

ok.log: You win by a single stone. He smiles and taps your chest twice. 'You breathe like you play: too fast.' He is right. Everything changes a little.

fail.log: He crushes you in forty moves, then pours you tea. 'Again next year,' he says.

effects.log: He plays both sides for an hour. Somehow, both sides lose. You think about it all week.

events.text: Bandits are massing to attack the county town, and the garrison captain is out of ideas. Someone mentions that you play Go.

ok.log: You flood the low road, feint with the militia and close the trap at the river. The bandits never reach the walls.

fail.log: The bandits do something you did not expect. The town holds, barely, and you are in the thick of it.

effects.log: The town holds without you, at a cost. You hear the bells for the dead from the next valley.

events.text: A child in the village has a fever that the local healer cannot break. The parents come to you because they heard you know herbs.

ok.log: Three nights of willow bark, cold cloths and a needle behind the ear. On the fourth morning the child asks for dumplings.

fail.log: You do what you can. The healer from the next town arrives in time. You study harder after that.

choices.text: Send them to the city physician

effects.log: You pay for the cart. The child lives. You wonder if you could have done it yourself.

events.text: The old poison still lives in your blood. With what you now know of medicine, you think you could brew a cure.

ok.log: Seven herbs, three days of simmering, one horrible cup. The numbness in your hands finally, completely, goes away.

fail.log: Close. Not close enough. You spend a week sweating it out.

effects.log: You tell yourself there will be time. There usually is. Usually.

events.text: On the road you find a wounded man in the black robes of the Demonic Cult. He is barely breathing, and he is very young.

ok.log: He wakes, stares at you, and says nothing. Before dawn he is gone. A black lotus is left folded on your pack. A debt, in their language.

fail.log: You try. He dies at dawn, holding your sleeve. You bury him under a pine.

effects.log: Behind you, the crows are already circling.

events.text: A thief snatches a widow's purse in the night market and vanishes up onto the rooftops.

ok.log: Three rooftops, one clothesline and a very surprised pigeon later, you land in front of him. The widow gets her purse back. The crowd applauds.

fail.log: You go through a roof instead of across it, into someone's kitchen. The thief escapes. The family feeds you anyway.

effects.log: The guards arrive, eventually. The thief is long gone.

variants: In the night market a thief grabs a widow's purse and is up on the rooftops before anyone can shout.

events.text: A rare Snow Lotus grows halfway down a sheer cliff, where no one could possibly reach it.

ok.log: You run down the cliff face as if it were a garden path, pluck the lotus and run back up. It glows faintly in your hands.

fail.deathCause: a fall from the Snow Lotus cliff
fail.log: The rock crumbles under your foot. A pine tree catches you, twenty feet down. You climb back up with nothing but bruises.

effects.log: Some treasures are meant to stay where they are. You tell yourself that on the whole walk home.

events.text: A wandering swordsman with a notched blade stops you on a bridge. 'I hear you are good with a sword,' he says. 'Show me.'

ok.log: Three exchanges. Then he steps back, sheathes his blade and bows. 'Good.' He leaves you a single note on footwork that changes everything.

fail.log: He disarms you in one move and kicks your sword back to you. 'Again, in five years.' You will be ready.

effects.log: He shrugs and walks on. You wonder all week what you might have learned.

variants: A wandering swordsman with a chipped blade blocks your way on a bridge. 'They say you know the sword,' he says. 'Show me.'

events.text: A famous smith agrees to forge you a sword, if you spend a month at the forge helping. His price is 150 taels and your patience.

ok.log: The smith watches you test the blade and nods. 'It knows you.' A good sword is half the fight.

fail.log: The sword is excellent. You are not yet worthy of it. You will grow into it.

effects.log: You keep your old blade. It has never complained.

events.text: Practising in a summer storm, you realise you can see every raindrop before it falls.

ok.log: For one breath, not a single drop touches you. Then you are soaked, laughing, and something in your swordsmanship has changed forever.

fail.log: You cut a lot of rain. The rain wins, as rain does. Still, you felt something.

effects.log: You stand in the storm until your mind is as clear as the sky after it.

events.text: Five drunk mercenaries decide the old tavern keeper owes them free wine.

choices.text: Put them out with your bare hands

ok.log: Five mercenaries, one door, one very tidy exit. The tavern keeper hangs a piece of the broken table on the wall in your honour.

fail.log: You get three of them out. The other two get you out. The keeper patches you up in the kitchen.

choices.text: Pay for their wine and let them leave

effects.log: They leave, loudly. The keeper refills your cup for free for the rest of the year.

events.text: The village children follow you everywhere, begging you to teach them 'real kung fu'.

choices.text: Teach them basic stances every morning

effects.log: Twenty children, one dusty yard, a lot of falling over. Years later, one of them becomes a famous swordsman and tells everyone where it began.
They groan. Later, the ones who can read are the ones who understand the manuals.

events.text: You are old now. Your hands shake a little, but when they hold a brush or a sword, they do not.

effects.log: It takes a whole winter. When it is done, your manual goes to the nearest library. Your name will outlive you.

choices.text: Paint the mountain you were born under

ok.log: It is the best thing you have ever made. Someone offers a fortune for it. You give it to a child instead.

fail.log: It is not the mountain you remember. It is the mountain as it is now. Maybe that is better.
